quiz.explain: javac compiles source code into platform-independent bytecode, stored in a .class file.

quiz.q: Which part turns bytecode into instructions for your computer?
quiz.explain: The JVM interprets the bytecode and JIT-compiles hot parts to machine code for the current platform.

options: No, single-file launch is new in Java 25
Yes, it compiles in memory and runs (JEP 330, since JDK 11)
quiz.explain: Single-file source-code launch has been final since JDK 11, so JDK 23 and JDK 25 behave the same.

quiz.q: This compiles. What happens when you run it?
options: It prints Start, then stops with ArithmeticException
quiz.explain: javac only checks the code; dividing an int by zero fails while the JVM runs it. The first line has already printed Start.

quiz.q: Does this compile when saved as Hello.java?
options: No, the class name does not match the file name
No, main must be in a public class
quiz.explain: Only a public class must match the file name. This class is not public, so javac compiles it into hello.class.

quiz.q: What does write once, run anywhere mean?
options: You only write code once in your career
The same bytecode runs unchanged on every platform with a JVM
Source code runs directly on any processor
javac runs only once per project
quiz.explain: Bytecode is platform-independent; every JVM can run it unchanged.
The java command wants the class name. java Hello.class fails with "Could not find or load main class Hello.class".

quiz.q: You run java Mini.java on JDK 23 (no flags). Mini.java contains only void main() { IO.println("hi"); }. What happens?
options: It prints hi, just like on JDK 25
Compile error: implicitly declared classes are a preview feature
It fails only because of IO.println
It asks which JDK to use
quiz.explain: On JDK 23 compact source files are a preview (JEP 477) and need --enable-preview. On JDK 25 the same file runs with no flags.

quiz.q: Which workflow should you use for a Hyperskill project in IntelliJ?
options: The classic public class, compiled by javac and run by java on JDK 23
quiz.explain: Hyperskill's checks run on JDK 23 and expect the classic style.

flashcards.front: What are the three stages of a Java program?
flashcards.back: Write source code, compile it to bytecode, run it on the JVM.
It compiles a .java file into bytecode in a .class file.
Platform-independent instructions in a .class file that only a JVM can run.
It loads bytecode and runs it, interpreting it or JIT-compiling it to machine code.

flashcards.front: What does write once, run anywhere mean?
flashcards.back: The same .class file runs unchanged on any computer with a JVM.

flashcards.front: Classic way to compile and run Hello.java?

flashcards.back: The java command wants the class name: java Hello.
It compiles in memory and runs at once, without writing a .class file.
No. It is JEP 330, available since JDK 11.
A compile error stops javac, so no .class file is made. A run-time error stops the JVM while the program runs.
